0.note: **For the chief musician** is an instruction about who should lead people in singing or playing music with this psalm. This could refer to the person in charge of music for temple worship. If your readers would not be familiar with this role, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [For the music director] or [For the worship leader]

**On a stringed instrument** refers to a type of stringed musical instrument used in worship. This may indicate how the psalm was to be accompanied. If your readers would not be familiar with this type of instrument, you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [To be accompanied by stringed instruments] or [With music from stringed instruments]

1.note: These two phrases, **Hear my cry, God** and **listen to my prayer**, mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [God, hear my cry; yes, listen to my prayer]

These are imperatives, but they communicate polite requests rather than commands. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. Alternate translation: [Please hear my cry, God; please listen to my prayer]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **prayer**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what I pray]

2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about where David calls from after the information about calling to God. Alternate translation: [I call to you from the end of the earth]

David is using **From the end of the earth** as a common expression to mean from a very distant or remote place. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [From a faraway place] or [From distant lands]

Here the **heart** represents where a person’s thoughts and feelings exist. David is speaking of his emotions as if they were physically weak. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when I am discouraged] or [when I feel weak]

The word that the ULT translates as **when** indicates that David calls to God at the same time as **my heart is faint**. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [at times when my heart is faint] or [during the times that my heart is faint]

David is speaking of God as if God were a high **rock** that David could climb up to reach safety from danger. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [to a place of safety that is like a high rock]

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. Alternate translation: [Please lead me to the rock]

3.q: הָיִ֣יתָ מַחְסֶ֣ה לִ֑⁠י מִגְדַּל־עֹ֝֗ז מִ⁠פְּנֵ֥י אוֹיֵֽב
3.note: The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [you are a refuge to me, you are a strong tower from the face of the enemy]

3.q: הָיִ֣יתָ מַחְסֶ֣ה לִ֑⁠י מִגְדַּל־עֹ֝֗ז מִ⁠פְּנֵ֥י אוֹיֵֽב
3.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [you are a refuge to me, indeed, you are a strong tower from the face of the enemy]

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because you are a refuge to me]

Here David is speaking as if God were a physical shelter. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you are a place of protection for me] or [you are a place of safety for me]

Here David is speaking as if God were a fortified **tower**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a fortress that protects me from the enemy]

David is using **from the face of** as a common expression to mean “away from the presence of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the enemy] or [when the enemy comes]

4.q: אָג֣וּרָה בְ֭⁠אָהָלְ⁠ךָ עוֹלָמִ֑ים אֶֽחֱסֶ֨ה בְ⁠סֵ֖תֶר כְּנָפֶ֣י⁠ךָ
4.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [Let me always live in your presence, taking refuge in the shelter of your wings]

Here David is speaking as if God’s presence and protection were a **tent** where he could stay as a guest. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in your presence] or [with you]

Here David is speaking as if God were a bird sheltering its young under its **wings**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [under your care] or [in your protection]
David is using this possessive form to mean the shelter that God’s wings provide. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in the shelter that your wings provide]

5.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because you, God, have listened to my vows]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **inheritance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what is passed to]

David is using this possessive form to mean the inheritance that belongs to those who fear God. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [what you give to those who fear your name]

Here, **your name** represents God’s reputation and character. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [who you are] or [your reputation]

6.note: The psalmist is using **Days upon days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “many days.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [May you add many days to the king’s lifetime]
The phrase **the king** refers to David himself, who is speaking of himself in the third person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [me, the king]
The pronoun **you** refers to God, while the pronoun **his** refers to the king. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [may you, God, add to the king’s years]
Here, **his years** represents “his lifetime.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to his lifetime]

The point of this comparison is that just as **generation and generation** spans a very long time, so should the king’s years be extended. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as if he would live for many generations]

David is using **to generation and generation** as a common expression of his culture to mean “throughout all generations” or “forever.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [throughout all generations]

7.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the king mentioned in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [May the king dwell forever]

Here, **to the face of God** represents being in the presence of God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the presence of God] or [before God]

The phrase **covenant faithfulness and truth** expresses a single idea. The word **truth** tells more about **covenant faithfulness**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [true covenant faithfulness] or [faithful covenant love]

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please appoint covenant faithfulness and truth]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **covenant faithfulness** and **truth**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [evidences that you are truly faithful to your covenant]

David speaks of **covenant faithfulness and truth** as if they were living things that could **preserve** the king. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [ways to show the king covenant faithfulness and truth so that he is preserved]

8.note: Here, **name** represents God himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to you]

The phrase **that I may pay my vows** indicates the purpose or goal for which David will make music to God’s name. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [in order to pay my vows day after day] or [so that I may pay my vows day after day]

David is using **pay my vows** as a common expression to mean “fulfill my vows” or “do what I have vowed to do.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [fulfill my vows] or [do what I have promised]

David repeats the word **day** to emphasize the idea of continually or constantly. If your language can repeat words for emphasis, it would be appropriate to do that here. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the emphasis. Alternate translation: [day after day] or [continually]
